previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was re-admitted due to a thrombosed left upper extremity AV graft, preventing dialysis access. A fistulogram and thrombectomy were attempted but were unsuccessful due to persistent stenosis in the graft. A temporary dialysis catheter was placed in the left internal jugular vein and later converted to a tunneled catheter. The patient received one dialysis session during admission and was stabilized. Chronic abdominal and left breast wounds were assessed; no abscess was found, and wound care was optimized for home management. The transplant surgery team will contact the patient to schedule outpatient graft repair. She was discharged home with visiting nurse services for wound care and instructions to resume regular dialysis through the tunneled catheter.
problems: Thrombosed left upper extremity AV graft

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o female who was taken to the OR with Dr ___ for 
attempted thrombectomy and revision of left upper arm AV graft. 
Per Dr ___ note, ""Based on the previous 
fistulogram, the hope
would have been that this was the proximal artery before the 
bifurcation, however, visualization of this artery demonstrated 
that this was already after the bifurcation and the artery 
proximal to the bifurcation could not be reached.
Given the fact that we have already had problems with inflow 
into this graft from this same artery, it was not felt 
worthwhile to try to create a new arterial anastomosis if it 
could not be done to the proximal artery.  Therefore, the
decision was made to abort this procedure. 

Post operatively, the patient was restarted on all home 
medications. It was discussed with patient that she has been 
unable to tolerate swallowing pills due to nausea and vomiting 
this created. She did attempt to take the long acting nitrate 
whole and experienced some vomiting. 
Due to cardiac history and post anesthesia status, CK and 
troponins were cycled, and were negative. An EKG did not show 
any changes from baseline.
Additionally, the isosorbide was changed from the long acting 
pill to TID short acting at a lower dose, as she is experiencing 
hypotension during HD.
These changes have been communicated to the PACT program 
following this patient.

able to complete a full run of HD, but due to hypotension, no

dwell of TPA, which was removed prior to her discharge to rehab.

Following HD, the patient was tolerating a regular diet.
The incision dressing was removed on POD 2. The incision is 
clean dry and sutures intact. There is no bruit and thrill as 
expected.

Per previous scheduled appointments as follow up for post

will have GYN follow up scheduled.

Regarding ongoing access issues, the patient has a follow up 
appointment with Dr ___, at which time further access 
potentially in the right arm will be discussed. The left arm 
graft will not be salvageable and for now will continue 
hemodialysis via the left tunneled HD catheter.

radiology_notes.text:
AP CHEST, 8:28 P.M., ___

HISTORY:  Attempt at open thrombosed graft, now with acute shortness of
breath.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___:

Lungs are better expanded, pulmonary vasculature has decreased.  There is no
focal pulmonary abnormality.  Severe cardiomegaly and pulmonary artery
enlargement are chronic.  No pneumothorax or pleural effusion.  Left
supraclavicular dual-channel dialysis catheters end in the right atrium.

HISTORY:  ___ female with vaginal bleeding of unclear etiology.

COMPARISON:  No previous ultrasound for comparison.

FINDINGS:

On transabdominal imaging the uterus is not well visualized due to the
patient's body habitus.  An endovaginal exam was performed for better
visualization of the endometrium and pelvic organs.  The uterus is retroverted
and measures 6.4 x 3.8 x 4.9 cm.  Numerous calcified fibroids are seen
scattered throughout the uterus.  The largest fibroid is in the posterior
margin of the uterus measuring 2.1 x 1.6 x 1.6 cm.  In the fundal segment of
the uterus the endometrium is minimally echogenic and enlarged measuring 6 mm.
An abnormality at this location cannot be excluded.

The ovaries could not be identified on images of the adnexa bilaterally.

IMPRESSION:

1. Minimally enlarged endometrium in the fundal segment.  A GYN consultation
is suggested and hysteroscopy or sonohysterogram could be performed to better
assess the endometrium.

2. Numerous small calcified fibroids are seen scattered throughout the uterus.

3. The ovaries could not be identified.
